leads.summary: Clean textual merge with open #13277 silently replaces About's logo override
leads.consequence: Both PRs target the same About wrapper. A three-way merge against their common base exits 0 without conflict markers, but retains two about_fastfetch definitions; the later definition from #13277 invokes fastfetch without --logo-type file --logo $LOGO_FILE. The packaged config from #12268 consequently runs its command-raw wordmark in About, not the user's about.txt; the landmark/sheen cannot find the branding file. The resulting launch-about test exits 1 at 'About draws the branding file rather than the terminal wordmark'. Reconcile the wrappers when integrating these PRs, keeping #13277's hint/config work and About's file-logo override. This is not a claim that #13277 is already merged.

leads.summary: Fallback's last-existing assumption fails when the duplicate checkout logos diverge
leads.consequence: The new list scans the share-tree compact O before the retained etc/fastfetch checkout copy, yet fallback=$file always takes the last existing path. On a dev-linked checkout where etc/fastfetch/logo-small.txt has been edited to a larger mark, a 40x12 terminal with neither mark fitting prints that large etc file rather than the smaller available default/fastfetch/logo-small.txt. In the isolated run the chosen output was a 75-column X line although the 14-column O exists. Stock, byte-identical copies are currently unaffected; the exposed boundary is a divergent editable checkout or other partial/corrupt file set. Derive fallback from actual dimensions or place fallback copies before canonical share files.
leads.triage: factual, confirmed by coordinator read of helper lines 61-83; folded into N1 Impact; Opus self-check rp4 reproduced

leads.summary: New packaged-layout fixture checks only 80 columns; a broken packaged 120-column choice passes
leads.consequence: The checkout has both etc/fastfetch and default/fastfetch copies, so its 120-column assertion can pass via the etc fallback even if the new package path for the medium variant is never read. The only new packaged-layout assertion checks 80 columns, using the separate small file. A derived helper that removes the packaged medium entry and reads etc/fastfetch/logo.txt before the share-tree small entry passes all of this test (exit 0), while a staged packaged layout at 120 columns displays the small O instead of the 8-row compact wordmark. Add a packaged-medium assertion (and ideally wide) to the new fixture.
leads.triage: dropped: mutant relies on checkout-only etc copies that N1 suggests removing; low value

leads.summary: Changed logo test fails before reaching the new package fixture under LC_ALL=C
leads.consequence: With LC_ALL=C the test calculates byte length for the Nerd Font/box-drawing string, yielding box_width=146 rather than 54. The script fails its first width assertion and never exercises the newly added packaged-layout assertion. This is an existing test/source locale issue, not a new production regression in commit 161045f4; it corroborates prior R1-F4. Force a UTF-8 locale for width measurements or use a locale-independent display-column counter.
leads.triage: factual, confirmed by coordinator read (test line 36-39, test/shell sets no locale) and Sol review.py run; Opus rp4/rp5 extended it (line_width); published within R1-F4

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12268#issuecomment-5833238635) after [the author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12268#issuecomment-5835494934), checked at `161045f`.

**Outcome:** **Verified:** the packaged-install logo finding is resolved, and the new commit adds no behavioural regression in the tested scope. The four other earlier findings are still present, since their code did not change. There is one new cleanup item, and a merge interaction with open PR #13277.

### Resolved: smaller logos on packaged installs

**Verified:** The `omarchy-settings` and `omarchy-settings-dev` recipes in `omacom/omarchy-pkgs` copy `default/` to `/usr/share/omarchy/default/`, and the helper now reads `$OMARCHY_PATH/default/fastfetch/logo.txt` and `logo-small.txt`. With a packaged layout staged by the recipes' own `package()` functions, the helper picks the compact O up to 102 columns, the half-width wordmark from 103 to 142, and the full wordmark from 143 (UTF-8 locale, 24 rows or more). fastfetch 2.68.1 in a pseudo-terminal, config's static box modules only:

| Terminal | Previous head, packaged layout | Current head, packaged layout |
|---|---|---|
| 80x24 | full wordmark, modules at columns 90 to 143, none visible | compact O, modules at 23 to 76, fits |
| 120x40 | full wordmark, modules at 90 to 143, clipped | half-width wordmark, modules at 50 to 103, fits |
| 160x40 | full wordmark, fits | full wordmark, modules at 90 to 143, fits |

- The new test case stages a layout with no `etc/` tree. With the previous helper it fails at exactly that case ("a packaged layout still picks the compact O at 80 columns").
- The earlier suggestion to fall back to the smallest logo rather than the last one is not implemented, but in both the packaged and checkout layouts the last file found is the compact O, so a terminal too small for any mark still gets the compact O.

### Still present (code unchanged)

- **About overrides a user's own fastfetch logo:** `about_fastfetch` still always passes `--logo-type file --logo "$LOGO_FILE"`.
- **`NO_COLOR` in `omarchy-ascii`:** auto mode still colours any terminal output regardless of `NO_COLOR`.
- **Locale-dependent width:** `logo_width` still uses `${#line}`. Now that packaged installs have the smaller logos, this reaches them too: with `LC_ALL=C` the packaged helper picks the compact O up to 162 columns and never picks the full wordmark up to 200 columns. The result is still smaller than needed, never larger. The test has the same dependency: its module-box check (`test/shell.d/fastfetch-logo-test.sh:39`) measures 146 under `LC_ALL=C` and the file stops there, and `test/shell` sets no locale. **Optional:** set `LC_ALL=C.UTF-8` for the helper's measurement, and export it at the top of the test so all of its width checks count characters (the test's `line_width` also uses `${#line}`).
- **Redirected fastfetch output:** the helper still colours unless `NO_COLOR` is set, and fastfetch passes those codes through to a file (confirmed from source only in this follow-up).

### The `etc/fastfetch` logo copies are unused

`etc/fastfetch/logo.txt` and `logo-small.txt` are byte-identical to the new `default/fastfetch/` copies. On a packaged install they are installed to `/etc/fastfetch/`, but the helper looks for them under `$OMARCHY_PATH/etc/fastfetch/` (`/usr/share/omarchy/etc/fastfetch/`), which does not exist. In a checkout, the `default/` entries come first and win whenever a logo fits. Removing both `etc` copies and helper lines 65 and 66 left all 23 tests passing and the same selection at 80, 120 and 160 columns in both layouts.

**Impact:** Two unused files ship to `/etc/fastfetch/`, and the two copies can drift apart. A change to only the `etc` copies shows only in a checkout, where the helper still scans them after the `default` ones. For example, the no-fit fallback there is `etc/fastfetch/logo-small.txt`, and a sandboxed run with a 30-column `etc` copy printed it in a 40-column terminal instead of the 14-column O.

**Suggested change:** Remove `etc/fastfetch/logo.txt`, `etc/fastfetch/logo-small.txt` and helper lines 65 and 66. The new comments also disagree with the code: line 73 says "Prefer the smallest known mark if nothing fits, not the last file scanned", but line 74 still keeps the last file scanned, and line 82 ("variants are largest→smallest") is not true while the `etc` half-width wordmark follows the `default` compact O. Removing the `etc` entries makes line 82 true; line 73 can be reworded, or the fallback can choose the smallest mark explicitly.

### Merge interaction with #13277

Open PR #13277 also defines `about_fastfetch` in `bin/omarchy-launch-about`, at a different position. The two PRs merge without a textual conflict, so the merged file has both definitions, and bash uses the later one:

Condensed from the merged file:

```text
line 26  about_fastfetch() { fastfetch --logo-type file --logo "$LOGO_FILE" "$@"; }   # this PR
line 85  about_fastfetch() { fastfetch [--config "$ABOUT_CONFIG"] "$@"; }            # #13277, wins
```

On a local merge of the two heads, this PR's `launch-about-test.sh` fails at "About draws the branding file rather than the terminal wordmark". #13277's `launch-about-test.sh` passes on its head.

**Impact:** Whichever PR lands second silently drops this PR's logo override. For users without their own fastfetch config, About would draw the command-raw terminal wordmark rather than `about.txt`, so the layout measurement would not find `about.txt` in the render and neither the window fit nor the sheen would run (the rendering effect is from source only).

**Suggested change:** When the second of the two lands, keep one `about_fastfetch` that applies both #13277's config selection and this PR's `--logo-type file --logo "$LOGO_FILE"` override.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the new commit, the unchanged files behind the earlier findings, the `omacom/omarchy-pkgs` recipes (at `e2bc758`) and the fastfetch 2.68.1 source. Sandboxed runs covered the PR's three shell tests on the current head (`fastfetch-logo-test.sh` 23, `ascii-test.sh` 25 and `launch-about-test.sh` 28 passing) and the previous head, the previous helper against the new test as a negative control, a packaged layout staged by running the recipes' `package()` functions under bash (not makepkg, x86_64 only), a helper size matrix in UTF-8 and C locales, fastfetch 2.68.1 in a pseudo-terminal with only the config's static box modules, mutation runs, and a local merge with the #13277 head. Screens were approximated from the byte stream. The About window was not run.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
